passage: Devika had just finished presenting her poster at the department seminar when Dr Manjula said from the back row, "A bit ambitious for a second-year, don't you think?" The room laughed. Two weeks earlier Manjula had praised the very same data. Since Devika's abstract was accepted for the national meeting, her lab-meeting slots had shrunk, and the shared microscope booking kept showing Manjula's name against her usual hours. Devika still remembered how Manjula taught her to read a blot, so she answered, "Thank you, Ma'am. I learnt to check my controls from you." Afterwards, in the corridor, she wondered what she had done wrong. On Friday she emailed Professor Rao, a visiting collaborator, asking for feedback on her next draft.

qa.q: What did Dr Manjula say about Devika's poster?
qa.a: Dr Manjula said it was a bit ambitious for a second-year.

qa.q: Why did Devika wonder what she had done wrong in the corridor?
qa.a: Devika was confused, since Manjula had praised the same data two weeks earlier and the change made no sense to her.

qa.q: What did Devika do to keep growing without shrinking?
qa.a: She thanked Manjula for what was taught and reached out to Professor Rao for feedback on her next draft.

qa.q: How might Manjula be feeling as Devika's abstract is accepted?
qa.a: Manjula may feel threatened or overshadowed, though the passage shows only behaviour, not the reason.

grounding: A mentor in a department seems threatened by a mentee's rise and undercuts her; the mentee stays respectful and seeks other guides.
